rows.title: Policy
rows.figure: Fed Oct 28 hold ~93%, Dec hike >80%; BoC Oct 28 hike ~75–80% (TD, Rabobank: hold); RBNZ Oct 28 hike ~87% (tonight 8:00 PM CT); ECB Oct 29 hold ~95%; BoJ Oct 30 hold ~98%; RBA Nov 3 ~50%; BoE Nov 5 hike ~94%
rows.read: Five central banks decide this week, starting with New Zealand tonight, and most still lean toward raising rates because energy keeps inflation high. Canada and New Zealand are expected to hike, while the Fed, the ECB and the Bank of Japan are expected to hold. Currencies barely moved overnight as investors waited.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: China industrial profits Sep +14.4% y/y (Aug 4.2%); South Korea Q3 GDP +1.0% q/q (0.7% fc); US durable goods Sep fc +0.6% (7:30 AM CT); US consumer confidence Oct fc 81.2 (9:00 AM CT)
rows.read: Asia's growth news was good: Chinese factory profits jumped and South Korea's economy beat expectations on chip exports. That helps commodity sellers like Australia a little. US spending and confidence figures today test whether the American economy is still strong enough for a December Fed hike.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Brent $115.15 (−0.6%); UK BRC shop prices Oct +2.1% y/y (1.6% fc); Japan services PPI Sep +3.7% (as expected); Australia Q3 CPI tonight 7:30 PM CT (trimmed ~+1.0% q/q fc)
rows.read: Energy is still the main reason inflation runs above target in most big economies. In Britain, shop prices are now rising at their fastest pace in about two and a half years as energy costs spread into everyday goods. Australia's inflation figures tonight are the week's first big test.

rows.title: Risk
rows.read: Markets stayed calm overnight: Asian stocks mostly rose, led by chipmakers, and regional talks with Iran went on. That kept demand for safe havens low, so the yen slipped again and the franc held still. Fresh attacks or failed talks would quickly reverse that.

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.figure: Brent $115.15 (−0.6%); WTI $100.80 (−0.9%); Houthi–Saudi exchanges continue; record month of ship attacks near Hormuz (Reuters)
rows.read: Oil eased only a little, so most of the war premium is still in the price. That keeps pressure on energy importers like Japan and the euro area and still supports Canada. Stronger Chinese factory profits are a small plus for Australia's raw-material exports.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 20: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against NZD (sharply added) and EUR (added), for GBP (real money strongly against), for AUD (real money strongly against), leaning against JPY (flipped), strongly for gold (trimmed)
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar and the kiwi, even though both central banks are expected to hike this week, so those bets are exposed if the hikes come with signals of more. In the pound and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: Moody's held France at Aa3, negative outlook (Oct 23); French revenue-section first reading postponed; UK Budget Wed Oct 28 ~7:30 AM CT
rows.read: Pressure on France has eased since Moody's held its rating, though the first parliamentary vote on France's budget revenues has been postponed. Britain's first Budget from Chancellor John Healey on Wednesday is the bigger test: heavier borrowing could unsettle UK bonds and the pound.
